transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-09-23 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO, Caelum), Evan (SRE, Caelum), Lena (Head of ML, Caelum)

Summary: discovery focused on dedicated capacity patterns — hotpool stickiness, tenant eviction during surge, pre-warm strategies, and data isolation requirements. Customer wants predictable p99 latency under bursty traffic while controlling costs and ensuring VPC/KMS compliance.

Topics: dedicated reserved nodes, warm/hot pool semantics, eviction/segmentation, routing fallback to hosted, telemetry and billing attribution, security (KMS/SOC2), timeline for PoC.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you carving time. i'm maya from redwood, i'm the ae on the account. with me is omar, our se. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya: good thanks, quick heads up, we have a hard stop at 15:50 pst, so 15:50 pst i think is 23:50 utc? sorry i got mixed up. but we 45 minutes ish.
[00:15] Evan: yep, we should be fine. excited to dig in — main ask is we need consistent p99 for inference regressions across bursts.
[00:21] Omar: cool, thanks. can i kick off with a quick run through of how redwood handles reserved pools and the warm/hot pools, then we'll map to your traffic?
[00:28] Priya: please do.
[00:31] Omar: okay, so the dedicated offering gives you reserved GPU capacity — it's essentially a pool of nodes you own, um, that we manage the runtime on. you can configure warm pool size and a hotpool threshold. warm pool we use for pre-warmed containers to reduce cold start; hotpool is sticky instances kept heated for low-latency tail. one note, in some transcripts our product was written as "redwood dedicatedee" or stuff, but that's just transcription.
[00:52] Lena: when you say sticky, do you mean sessions are pinned to a particular GPU for the full conversation? or sticky in the sense of cache locality?
[01:00] Omar: good question. sticky is primarily cache locality — we keep the kv cache and model kernel state co-located to avoid reloading token context. session pinning can be enabled if you need long-lived state, but it raises blast radius for noisy tenants.
[01:15] Priya: right, our main concern is p99 under bursts. sometimes we see a sudden 5x QPS spike and everything tails badly. we need a plan where critical tenants never get evicted during spikes.
[01:26] Maya: makes sense. quick qual — how many concurrent tenants and request profiles? are you multi-tenant today or already shard-per-tenant?
[01:33] Evan: we run about 120 active tenants, but the top 10 produce ~70% of traffic. currently it's multi-tenant on bigcloud endpoints, we are exploring moving to dedicated to reduce noisy neighbor effects.
[01:44] Lena: model sizes vary — most are 7B and 13B; a few experimental 70B for internal research but not prod-facing. typical sequence length is 512 tokens.
[01:53] Omar: cool, that helps. so two levers — reserve more capacity for dedicated pools and configure hotpool stickiness to protect those top tenants. eviction policies can be strict (never evict pinned tenants) or soft (evict warm pool first).
[02:07] Priya: what's the cost delta we should expect between a fully pinned tenant strategy vs soft eviction?
[02:12] Maya: rough ballpark: pinned-per-tenant increases reserved GPU needs by ~20–40% depending on number of heavy tenants. soft eviction with fast pre-warm and prefix caching will cut p99 without doubling capacity, but it's workload dependent. we'll share a sizing worksheet.
[02:27] Evan: can you elaborate on the pre-warm timings? we observed prewarm failing when burst exceeds expected ramp.
[02:34] Omar: right — pre-warm is based on traffic prediction windows and a budget. we support aggressive pre-warm where we hold warm containers longer which increases cost. there's also a rapid burst pattern: if upstream spikes beyond pre-warm, we fall back to autoscale from shared pool or hosted fallback. that fallback introduces a small p99 bump.
[02:53] Priya: fallback to hosted — is that acceptable for us? we have compliance needs, some data can't leave our vpc.
[02:59] Maya: important callout — you can configure fallbacks per-route. for sensitive routes we won't fallback to hosted; instead we'll prioritize billed reserved nodes or return backpressure. for non-sensitive flows you can tolerate fallback to hosted for short windows.
[03:14] Evan: okay that's helpful. about isolation — we need KMS integration and audit logs for every inference. do you expose per-tenant encryption keys?
[03:22] Omar: yes, in private deployment we integrate with KMS/HSM; for dedicated we support customer-managed keys via our KMS connectors (we had some earlier notes mis-transcribed as "K M S S"), and we emit audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud pubsub.
[03:36] Lena: are logs tokenized? we can't have PII in logs.
[03:40] Maya: logs are metadata-only by default; full payloads are opt-in and can be redacted. we also support field-level masking through our ingestion hooks.
[03:49] Priya: one more on eviction — can you do soft eviction by tenant priority? e.g., protect paid tier A, degrade tier B/C?
[03:56] Omar: yep, we have policy-based routing where priority classes map to eviction weight. The runtime marks tenants with sticky score; when reclaiming, lower weight tenants are evicted from hotpool first.
[04:08] Evan: how do you measure stickiness effectiveness? do you have metrics to show cache hit rate and tail latency per-tenant?
[04:15] Maya: console has per-route/persist-level dashboards: p50/p95/p99, kv cache hit rate, prefix cache stats, token cost. SEs can instrument custom traces to break down per-tenant tail.
[04:26] Priya: can we test this in a poc — like run synthetic bursts and validate that top tenants retain under 200ms p99?
[04:33] Omar: absolutely. our usual poc is 2–3 weeks: baseline tests on your traffic, then we apply reserved topology with hotpool policy, run chaos bursts, and measure. we can also run a compliance checklist for VPC and KMS.
[04:45] Priya: timeline wise, we'd like to decide by mid-october. procurement might want a cost model.
[04:51] Maya: understoood. we'll put together a pricing matrix for reserved tiers + warm-pool options.
[04:56] Evan: about warm-pool stickiness — if a tenant is evicted and then returns, is there a cooldown where they can't get re-pinned? we want to avoid flapping.
[05:03] Omar: we have a cooldown window and a score decay. the system uses an LRU-ish, but with weights and decay to prevent thrashing. the score considers recent hit-rate, token usage, and SLA tier.
[05:15] Lena: curious about multi-model workloads: if the same GPU hosts two different model families, do you have interference?
[05:21] Omar: yes there is cross-model interference; our kernel scheduler isolates memory and pins highest-priority model to dedicated memory partitions, but if you have heavy 70B and a 13B at the same time you can see performance cliffs. for that we recommend model packing rules or separate pools.
[05:36] Priya: i noticed in another vendor's docs they recommend overprovisioning by 50% to avoid evictions—seems expensive. can redwood do smarter packing to reduce that?
[05:45] Maya: that's a common pattern. our runtime uses a packing optimizer that considers sequence length distribution and kernel footprint. typically we reduce the naive overprovision by 15–30% depending on variability.
[05:56] Evan: security/compliance — SOC2 docs, network diagrams?
[06:00] Maya: yes we'll send SOC2 and our security pack; for private/dedicated we'll provide network architecture diagrams for VPC peering or on-prem connectors.
[06:08] Priya: can you do a live demo of eviction in the poc? like show eviction events in real-time?
[06:13] Omar: yes, we can instrument the console with live eviction stream and traces. note that the console will sometimes show weird abbreviations — e g it might surface as "evict-job" or "seg-reclaim" depending on infra logs.
[06:25] Priya: fair. latency SLO — we want p99 < 200ms for top tenants, p95 < 80ms for the rest. feasible?
[06:32] Omar: for 7B/13B on A100-ish hardware with sticky hotpool you can hit that in most cases for short sequences. sequences of 512 will push it, so we'd profile your traces.
[06:43] Evan: what's the typical warm-to-hot transition time?
[06:46] Omar: warm-->hot is sub-second for a cached kv snapshot; cold start from scratch is more like 10–20s for large models.
[06:53] Lena: do you support quantized variants to reduce GPU memory?
[06:56] Omar: yes we recommend int8/4 quant for 13B+ and have verified kernels for common open models. quantization helps packing and reduces eviction pressure.
[07:06] Priya: are there any gotchas with quantized models for our use-case? we use a few generation patterns that rely on exact logits.
[07:12] Maya: quant can slightly impact quality; part of the poc can be a quality check using your eval prompts. we surface regression alerts in Redwood Optimize.
[07:21] Evan: we want billing attribution per-tenant, per-route — do you emit token-level cost?
[07:27] Maya: yes per-token cost and token counts per-route in the console. you can export per-tenant billing reports.
[07:33] Priya: good. ok, quick exercise — if we wanted to guarantee no eviction for top 10 tenants for 99% of bursts, what's the approach?
[07:41] Omar: approach: 1) identify top 10 baseline footprints (model + seq dist) 2) reserve a hotpool sized to hold them all pinned simultaneously + a warm buffer 3) set eviction policy to never evict pinned top-tier 4) enable aggressive pre-warm for minutes around expected spikes 5) fallback = backpressure for sensitive routes 6) monitor with p99 alarms and auto-escalation.
[08:00] Maya: i'll add that we can run a simulation against your traces to recommend exact hotpool size. we'll need those traces.
[08:06] Evan: noted. any limitations on on-prem vs vpc for this setup?
[08:11] Omar: on-prem gives you total control and KMS/HSM integration is direct; VPC redwood-managed dedicated is simpler but requires peering and our control plane still coordinates. both support the hotpool/eviction controls.
[08:24] Priya: procurement question — minimum commitment or term?
[08:28] Maya: dedicated reserved nodes typically require a monthly commit; we have quarterly and annual pricing and can tailor. we'll send details in the pricing sheet.
[08:36] Lena: for the poc, would you expect any agents onsite? or is it fully remote?
[08:41] Maya: fully remote is fine; SE-led remote bench. if you want onsite assistance during cutover we can scope that as professional services.
[08:49] Evan: one operational question — if a pinned tenant gets disabled, do you immediately reclaim and reassign the hot slot?
[08:54] Omar: we have configurable reclaim policies; immediate reclaim is possible but we usually do graceful drain with a short cooldown.
[08:59] Priya: ok, last thing — are there any recent incidents where hotpool stickiness failed? curious for postmortem learnings.
[09:06] Omar: there was an incident last q where an autoscaler bug allowed thrash between warm and hot pools during a cascading spike; we patched it and added a score-stabilizer. we'll share a summarized incident note.
[09:19] Maya: we'll attach that note.
[09:21] Priya: great. i think that's most of our questions. can we recap next steps?
[09:26] Maya: sure — action items: send sizing worksheet & pricing (maya), caelum to share traces (evan), omar to draft canary/fallback playbook. schedule poc kickoff for early october.
[09:37] Evan: yep will aim to get traces by sept 29.
[09:40] Lena: i'll be available for eval prompts and quality checks.
[09:43] Maya: perfect. thanks everyone, i'll follow up with a calendar invite for a poc kickoff and upload security pack.
[09:49] Priya: thanks, bye.

Recap (auto): Redwood to provide warm/hot sizing worksheet, pricing tiers, SOC2/security pack, and simulation offer. Caelum to provide traffic traces and eval prompts. Plan: 2–3 week poc, simulate bursts and validate p99 for top tenants.
